subject: Future Tech
title: Lunar and Martian Construction
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Lunar and Martian Construction.

hook.text: NASA and ESA plan to 3D-print bases on the Moon using lunar regolith. No need to ship bricks 240,000 miles from Earth.

buildup.text: Robots would arrive first, scoop lunar soil, and mix it with binder to print walls that shield against radiation.

discovery.text: AI SpaceFactory won a NASA contest with a Mars habitat design that a robot can print autonomously without human help.

twist.text: Martian regolith contains perchlorates—toxic chemicals that complicate its use as building material and need treatment.

climax.text: NASA and China's space agency have committed to printing the first permanent structures beyond Earth by the 2030s.

punchline.text: The first home on the Moon will come from a printer.

quiz.question: What toxic challenge does Martian regolith present for construction?
